title: 2027-07-19-nautilus-retail-implementation-kickoff-and-integration-planning
transcript:
Header:
- Date/Time: 2027-07-19 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 1h05m (approx)
- Meeting type: Implementation kickoff / onboarding intake
- Record: Fireflies auto-transcript (medium quality)
- Shared artifacts: Kickoff deck https://redwood.link/nautilus-kickoff-deck, security packet https://redwood.link/nautilus-security, benchmark sheet (view-only) https://sheets.redwood/naut-bench

Summary:
Quick intro kickoff to align implementation scope for Nautilus Retail pilot. Discussed integration touchpoints (API vs private VPC), success criteria for pilot (latency < 200ms P95 for storefront autofill, cost target <$0.002/token), security requirements (SOC2/SSO/KMS), and next steps: infra deep-dive, runbook delivery, scheduling a dedicated perf test window.

Topics covered:
- Onboarding timeline and milestones (pilot -> staging -> prod)
- Network topology: hosted API vs Private (VPC) deployment options
- Data handling and retention, KMS integrations, audit logs
- Performance expectations and benchmark plan (inventory autocomplete workload)
- Rollout plan and stakeholders for success criteria

Auto-detected action items (in-call):
- Sophie to share onboarding runbook and SDK snippets (link + checklist)
- Liam to schedule perf/infra deep-dive with Nautilus infra team and propose test window
- Evan to provide security questionnaire answers and sample audit requirements

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sophie Ramos: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sophie, I'll be your CSM for the Nautilus pilot. We also have Liam from Solutions. Uh, before we jump in, quick intros?
[00:18] Maya Chen: Hi, I'm Maya, Head of ML. We're leading the model integration side.
[00:22] Carlos Rivera: Carlos, platform, I'll be implementing the API and network stuff.
[00:28] Priya Nair: Priya, product manager, running the pilot outcomes and success metrics.
[00:33] Evan Brooks: Evan, security architect, I'll be owning compliance questions.
[00:36] Liam Patel: Liam here, SE at Redwood. I'll handle the perf plan, infra details, and the demo bits.

[02:05] Sophie Ramos: Cool. Goal for today is to map out the first 6 weeks — what we need to configure, who touches what, and lock a perf window. Does that align with what you expected?
[02:18] Priya Nair: Yes, that's right. We want a small pilot for the storefront autocomplete and product re-rank. Timeline is aggressive — we'd like a staging run in 5 weeks if possible.

[03:02] Liam Patel: Okay, good. Quick question on architecture: are you leaning to use Redwood-hosted API or do you need a private VPC/on-prem deployment for e2e data residency?
[03:18] Carlos Rivera: For the pilot we can probably start hosted, but we need VPC options later. Also we've got internal restrictions around PII and logs, so any request/response retention has to be configurable.

[04:10] Evan Brooks: We also have a KMS requirement — keys must be customer-managed, HSM is a plus. SOC2 audits are mandatory for production.
[04:26] Sophie Ramos: That's expected. Redwood supports customer KMS integrations and we have a private deployment path. I'll attach the security packet after the call.

[05:40] Maya Chen: On model side: we want to use an open LLM variant and possibly quantize for cost. We're concerned about latency for short completions—should be under 200 ms P95.
[05:58] Liam Patel: Right. There's a tradeoff between model size/quantization and latency. Our Optimize suggestions can pick quant profiles and batching. For autocomplete, continuous batching and prefix KV cache are important.

[07:45] Carlos Rivera: How intrusive is the KV cache? Will we need to manage cache invalidation and infra?
[07:52] Liam Patel: The runtime handles KV caching at the serving layer. You can configure TTLs, and we provide hooks to purge on deploys or product catalog updates. There's a small client-side pin that helps with warm starts.

[09:50] Priya Nair: Success criteria — from product: 1) latency target, 2) <1% regression vs current heuristics in conversion lift, 3) rollout with feature flagging and safe fallback.

[11:12] Sophie Ramos: Noted. We'll produce a pilot success checklist. We'll also propose an A/B rollout strategy and can run a canary with automatic fallback to heuristics.

[13:05] Maya Chen: For benchmarking, can Redwood run a perf test using a representative workload? We can share sample traces and QPS numbers.
[13:22] Liam Patel: Yes, we'll run a perf sweep in a reserved test window. Ideally we get your sample logs and query distribution, then we'll run P95/P99 latency profiles and token cost estimates.

[15:40] Evan Brooks: A practical security question: do you keep full request logs? We need to ensure minimal retention and redaction for PII. Also need audit log exports to our SIEM.
[15:54] Sophie Ramos: Redwood can configure retention and redaction rules. Audit logs can be exported to your S3 or sent via syslog to your SIEM. I'll include the audit log examples in the security packet.

[18:30] Carlos Rivera: Network-wise — for hosted: we need IP allow lists and TLS cert pinning; for private: VPC peering and direct connect are possibilities. Any constraints we should plan for?
[18:44] Liam Patel: We'll document supported topologies. For private: VPC endpoints with customer-managed subnets, and we support partner VPN/direct connect. For hosted: allow-lists and VPC egress proxies to restrict traffic.

[22:10] Priya Nair: Can you share SDK examples for our stack? We're primarily Node.js/Go on the platform side.
[22:22] Sophie Ramos: Yes — Node and Go SDK snippets will be in the runbook. Also we'll include a Postman collection and quickstart templates.

[25:00] Maya Chen: One concern — model versioning and rollbacks. How do we pin model versions and do canary traffic splits?
[25:12] Liam Patel: You can pin model versions per route, set rollout percentages, and define automatic rollback if latency or quality regressions are detected. Our console shows token-level cost and per-route latency.

[28:35] Evan Brooks: On compliance, we may require an on-site audit later. Do you offer audit support / SOC2 cert evidence?
[28:44] Sophie Ramos: Yes, we provide SOC2 reports on request and can coordinate a scoping call with our security team. I've put the request flow in the security doc link.

[32:00] Carlos Rivera: For the perf window, what do you need from us to simulate realistic QPS?
[32:08] Liam Patel: Sample query distribution, average tokens per request, and expected concurrency. If you can export 24 hours of anonymized traffic, that's ideal. We'll then plan a reserved test and share a tuning doc.

[36:40] Priya Nair: Timeline re-check — we said staging run in ~5 weeks. What are critical path items?
[36:50] Sophie Ramos: Critical path: 1) infra access + allow-lists, 2) security questionnaire returned, 3) sample traces for perf, 4) Redwood runbook + SDK integration. If those move fast we can hit the target.

[40:05] Maya Chen: One last item — cost target. We want sub $0.002 per token equivalent for the workload. Can Redwood provide estimated unit economics?
[40:17] Liam Patel: We'll produce a cost estimate in the benchmark sheet after we see sample traces. Our Optimize recommendations will include quantization and batching levers to meet that target.

[44:22] Sophie Ramos: Alright. Quick recap and owners — I'll go first. We'll send the onboarding runbook, post-call: deck, runbook, and security packet. Liam will schedule an infra deep-dive and a perf window. Maya/Carlos will share sample traces and infra constraints. Evan will return the security questionnaire. Priya — you'll confirm product success metrics and the pilot cohort.

[46:00] Maya Chen: Sounds good.
[46:10] Carlos Rivera: We'll aim to have sample traces and a first pass on CORS/IP allow-lists by next Tuesday.
[46:22] Evan Brooks: I'll try to get the security questionnaire back within 4 business days.
[46:30] Sophie Ramos: Great — we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the infra deep-dive.

[60:50] Meeting end: thanks everyone.

Notes about transcription quality: occasional misrecognitions ("Reedwood" for Redwood, "quantis-ation" for quantization), timestamps approximate.
